clinician.trajectory_summary: A 12-year-old boy presented with chronic mild right-sided chest pain and a non-resolving chest x-ray shadow. Chest CT revealed a well-defined, thin-walled cystic lesion in the right lower lobe. Surgical biopsy yielded histopathological confirmation of a bronchogenic cyst lined by respiratory epithelium with seromucinous glands, cartilage, and smooth muscle. No additional physical exam findings or clinical course details were documented.
